clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text and the held later orders EO 9323, EO 10444 and EO 14085 section 2, read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog: 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121) prints the order as amended through EO 14085 as current text with no ending statement; no held instrument revokes or supersedes it.

later_events.mechanism: amendment: section restated to read as follows (signed March 31, 1943); before, Army enlisted men completing three years with commander recommendation under regulations of the Secretary of War; after, Army enlisted men who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years or after December 7, 1941 served one year in wartime, no recommendation requirement; substance changed

amendment: restated to read as follows (signed April 10, 1953); before, Army only under the Secretary of War; after, Army and Air Force under the Secretaries of the Army and the Air Force, authority as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces, adds service after June 27, 1950 of less than three years, and a one-year minimum proviso; substance changed
amendment: strike and insert (section 2, signed October 3, 2022); men becomes members and the Space Force is added with eligibility dates on or after December 20, 2019 for Space Force members

clauses.reason: The paragraph establishes the Good Conduct Medal and authorizes its award to enlisted members under regulations of the service Secretaries. Before EO 9323: Army enlisted men who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal service and are recommended by their commanders, regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 9323: restated; Army enlisted men who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years, or after December 7, 1941 served one year during war; no commander recommendation; regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 10444: restated; authority as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces; regulations by the Secretaries of the Army and the Air Force; Army and Air Force enlisted men; adds those with less than three years of honorable service after June 27, 1950 who were not previously awarded the medal; proviso against awards for less than one year except physical-disability separations. After EO 14085 section 2: men becomes members and Space Force is added with a December 20, 2019 start for Space Force members. The clause was amended, never ended, and the U.S. Code prints the amended text as current, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (6 FR 3209), Good Conduct Medal, is a single operative paragraph in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8809.txt; trailing number [No. 8809], signed Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House June 28, 1941): a Good Conduct Medal is established and may be awarded, under regulations of the Secretary of War, to enlisted men of the Army of the United States who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal military service and are recommended by their commanding officers. Three later orders each amend that single clause and are recorded as later events with before and after text: EO 9323 (March 31, 1943) restated the paragraph; EO 10444 (April 10, 1953) restated it again; and EO 14085, section 2 (October 3, 2022) struck and inserted words. The OFR catalog record for EO 8809 reads 'Amended by: EO 9323, March 31, 1943; EO 10444, April 10, 1953 | See: Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163)'. Both Amended by notes are addressed as later events. The See note is a cross reference to a Secretary of Defense transfer order whose text is not held; it is not a revocation note, it predates EO 10444 (which already names the Secretary of the Air Force), and I do not treat it as ending or changing the order. EO 14085, which the catalog does not list, is found in held texts and in the U.S. Code note. Search of held texts for the number EO 8809 finds the order, EO 9323, EO 10444 (and the duplicate page text under EO 10445 and EO 9324), EO 14085 and the 1989 codification; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog report machine hits (the OFR catalog amendment notes for EO 9323 and EO 10444, the text of EO 14085, and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note prints the order as amended by EO 9323, EO 10444 and EO 14085 section 2, as current text; the printed current text matches the text as restated by EO 10444 and amended by EO 14085. The order's own text states no end date or condition. Substance changed across the restatements; a reviewer should read the before and after wording in the later events. The clause is operative as of 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: No clause is terminated, so no savings or residual question arises. The 1941 and 1943 wording is superseded by the later restatements as amendments, not ends; awards made under earlier wording are not claimed as residual effects of an exhausted command.
